Title: "Concealed Weapon" and "Disguised Weapon" (but real Q's too :) )

Messages.Author: Jozxyqk
Messages.Body:
What is the point of Concealed Weapon?
Disguised Weapon does the exact same thing, but better.

Concealed Weapon [Jyhad]
Cardtype: Combat
Discipline: Obfuscate
Equip this minion with a weapon card from your hand at the beginning of a round. Pay weapon's
equip cost from blood pool, as normal. The weapon cannot cost more than 2 pool or do more than 4
damage.

Disguised Weapon [Jyhad, V:TES, Sabbat, SW]
Cardtype: Combat
Discipline: Obfuscate
Only usable before range is chosen if you have a weapon card in your hand. Equip this vampire with
that weapon (and pay cost to equip as normal). (S) As above, but usable when choosing a strike.

Er.. after cutting and pasting from the site, I realize that Concealed Weapon
was immediately discontinued, so perhaps it answers my question.

But, perhaps Concealed Weapon was intended to be a disciplineless card?

Anyway, it's wallpaper now.
Although (remembering one of my previous posts), I think it would be hilarious
and shocking to create a deck based around Concealed Chainsaws... :)

Hmm.. this brings up another legitimate question, though..

Can a minion hold multiple weapons, and use different "only use once" weapons
for different strikes (Additional Strikes in the same round)?
i.e. Can I wear two Brass Knuckles, and punch twice?

This is a subject-path that has been walked down before. Even though the WotC
have stated that the card was intended to be a discipline-less, it has been
previously posted that creating errata to improve a card would not occur.
Though I can understand the reasoning for the rule, I am personally hoping
that eventually White-Wolf will create a card that makes Concealed Weapon
meet what it was initially intended, a disciplineless card. There has been
some suggested inputs that is Concealed Weapon was brought out this way, it
should also have some limits placed upon it to prevent abuse. One limit has
been to make the weapon in question be non-unique, thus an Ivory Bow could
not be acquired via Concealed Weapon but a Stake or .44 Magnum could.

My personal take is in favor of this type of limit if the card reprinted in a
future set. If not Final Nights, then maybe in a future set reprinting the
Camarilla clans.

Which probably makes a case for a (potentially virtually identical -
"Very Hidden Weapon", "Not Easily Seen Weapon") different card being
printed. Any number of different mechanics can work with it, not just
combat - an action modifier after a successful equip action, a combat
card restricted to certain phases of combat, an action card (equip
with a weapon from your hand, this action does not tap you) or
whatever.

I'm tempted to make the action "free" (a free untap), myself, simply
because I like Obfuscate still having the bite of surprise value.

> future set. If not Final Nights, then maybe in a future set reprinting the
> Camarilla clans.

It would make some sense in FN. The Ravnos do a few nice tricks with
equipment occassionally, though the Assamites have Disguised Weapon at
their disposal for Bang Nakh or whatever.

I know that WotC and WW have a tendency to errata and tone down power cards and
not to help out or improve wallpapered cards.

But I'm curious about some of the "changes" made for Sabbat War.

Yeah, some of them did limit cards. Legacy of Pander was neutered and many
cards were reworded to prevent stacking. So this seems consistent with toning
down (instead of toning up).

But how about other situations? Blood Brother Ambush and Ghouled Street Thug
were given strength. They helped improve Aggressive Tactics by eliminating the
Sabbat requirement. Superior Enchant Kindred was given the +1 stealth. And
requirements for Orgy of Blood and War Party were lightened up.

So what gives? It's not as if these were misprints or the toning down of cards.
Instead, it seems that White Wolf actually did hep improve less useful cards.
It could be argued that some of these changes would be appropriate logical or
thematically, or this was done to follow the designer's intent, but then the
same arguments could be made for Concealed Weapon.

So...doesn't the improvement of some wallpapered (and some non-wallpapered)
cards in Sabbat War set a strong precedent for doing the same for Concealed
Weapon?

Halcyan 2
